newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Stock Exchange monthly report for Sept.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Stock Exchange monthly report for Sept.

text.p: The monthly report is provided by the research department of the Philippine Stock Exchange.

Bearish sentiments prevailed over the market for the month of September despite developments in the local front. The government's announcement of a positve real GNP growth of 7.06 percent and the slowing down of the inflation rate in August to 7.90 percent failed to enliven the local equities market.
External factors such as the U.S.-Iraq blitz, the impending U.S.-interest rate hike and the unfavourable performance of other Asian bourses weighed down the Philippine stock market.

Taking its cue from the highly volatile Dow Jones Industrial Average, the PSE Composite Index plunged a hefty 50.93 index points as it closed lower at 3,169.78 index points from 3,220.71 posted last month.

Jittery over these external setbacks and the poor performance of the local stock market, fund managers and investors hugged the sidelines and opted not to take aggressive positions as total value turnover declined by over 1.13 billion pesos, or 2.42 percent, to 45.77 billion pesos.

The Commercial-Industrial (C-1) sector likewise displayed an unimpressive performance as profit-taking cut gains among blue-chip and second-line issues. The C-1 index ended the month at 4,294.53 points, a 1.25 percent decrease from the prior month's 4,348.96 points.
Oil refinery giant Petron Corporation lost 9.52 percent as it closed at 9.50 pesos.
Both "A" and "B" issues of Meralco slumped 2.83 percent and 3.48 percent, respectively, to close at 103 pesos and 194 pesos.

San Miguel Corporation, which has recently acquired a new licencing agreement with American brewer Miller Brewing Company to produce and distribute Miller Geniune Draft in the Philippine market, lost 3.66 percent in its "A" issues which closed at 39.50 pesos while its "B" issues gained a measly 0.58 percent to 86 pesos.

The property counter, which hugged the spotlight during the past months, is currently suffering a decline during the month in review as several analysts predicted that its bubble is about to burst with an impending oversupply scenario by the year 1998.
Megaworld Properties suffered a decline of 6.82 percent to close the month at 10.25 pesos from 11 posted last month.
Highly capitalized issue Ayala Land, Inc. "B" lkewise ended the month at 32 pesos, slipping 4.48 percent.

The property index closed at 164.39 points from last month's 169.20 points suffering a decline of 2.48 points. The mining counter likewise shed 127.48 points or 4.16 percent as it closed the month at 2,934.25 points.
Despite the unimpressive performance of the other sectors, speculative issues, particularly in the oil sector, provided the excitement on the trading floor.
The Oil counter closed 5.05 percent higher to close the month at 6.86 points.
Renewed buying interest in the Oil sector was evident as total volume turnover for this sector leaped by 178.77 percent from 93.85 billion to 261.63 billion registered last month.
Value turnover likewise surged 217.28 percent to 5.56 billion pesos.

APC Group, Inc. (APC), Sinophil Corporation (SINO) and Cophil Exploration Corporation (CXV) were among this month's favored issues as positive corporate developments triggered brisk trading among investors.

APC's share price shot up by 36 percent to 0.034 peso per share from the prior month's 0.025 peso. The Company's Board of Directors has recently approved the increase of the Company's authorized capital stock from 1.80 billion pesos to 20 billion.
The Company also confirmed its plan to change its par value from one centavo to 1.0 peso as well change their primary purpose from oil exploration to holdings.

Sinophil share prices, on the other hand, rose by as much as 50 percent from 0.012 peso to 0.018 peso per share with the approval of the Securities and Exchange Commission of its plan to double its authorized capital stock to 2.0 billion pesos.
Cophil Exploration garnered a 14.29 percent increase as share prices of the oil issues closed at 0.0160 peso from last month's 0.0140 peso.

CXC has announced that its Board of Directors has approved its plan to change its purpose into a holding company. Cophil is set to invest 65 million pesos for a 51 percent equity in Express Savings Bank and 229 million pesos for a 6.29 percent equity in Petrochemical Corporation of Asia Pacific.
The second phase of the company's restructuring involves a joint venture project with large Japanese groups in the development of a 200-hectare property in Cavite into an industrial estate.

The succesful listing of two new issues Ever Gotesco Resources and Holdings and Music Semiconductors Corporation in the local bourse provided a much needed shot in the arm for the languidly performing IPO market.

Holding company, Ever Gotesco Resources and Holdings Inc which listed 5 billion share with an offer of 1.0 peso per share appreciated by as much as 14 percent to 1.14 pesos. High-technology stock Music Semiconductors likewise chalked-up a 12.70 percent gain in share prices as it closed at 7.80 pesos on its listing day from an offer prices of 6.30 pesos.

The secondary offering of newly restructured holding company, Solid Group Inc which was formerly known as United Paracle Mining, likewise posted a gain of 7.69 percent to close its listing day at 6.30 pesos from an offering price of 5.85 pesos.
